episodes.168634: Two clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved west out of Georgia into Alabama, including north Alabama, during the afternoon and evening hours.  The thunderstorms were strong enough to knock down trees in Madison County during the afternoon and Marshall County during the evening hours.
episodes.168635: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of June 16th across a very warm and humid unstable airmass across Ontario and moved east across far northern NY into the Champlain Valley. Isolated to scattered reports of damaging wind occurred.
episodes.168636: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of June 16th across a very warm and humid unstable airmass across Ontario and moved east across far northern NY into the Champlain Valley, reaching Franklin county as a rogue isolated thunderstorm with some large hail.
episodes.168643: Scattered thunderstorms developed near the mountains, and a lee side surface trough, to the north and then shifted south and organized into a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) that produced strong damaging winds and some hail across the Midlands of SC, along with locally heavy rain and flooding in the Columbia metropolitan area, in the afternoon and evening.
episodes.168703: A new mesoscale convective system (MCS) developed from the outflow of a previously mature MCS in southern Wisconsin before venturing southeast into the Ohio River Valley the evening of June 13th. Strong winds from Indiana to eastern Ohio were measured and observed; the Fort Wayne International Airport in the state of Indiana measured a wind gust of 98mph. ||The county that was hit the hardest was Tuscarawas, as a rear inflow jet advances from the northwest. Drones, a damage survey team, and aerial satellite data (Sentinel 2) showed numerous swaths of tree damage in central Tuscarawas County. Isolated areas  experienced wind damage equivalent to an EF2 tornado (wind gusts up to 120mph).
episodes.168706: A broken line of supercells formed on the evening of June 16th as a mid-level trough interfered with agitated cumulus clouds in northwestern Ohio and a lake breeze east of Lake Erie. Moderate to high instability and high wind shear, 35-45kts and 1500-2500J/kg, helped with robust convection.
episodes.168707: A broken line of supercells formed on the evening of June 16th as a mid-level trough intersected a lake breeze east of Lake Erie. Moderate instability and high wind shear, 35-45kts and 1500-2500J/kg, helped with severe convection.
episodes.168939: Thunderstorms produced scattered instances of damaging winds and large hail, some considerable, across extreme eastern West Virginia into northern and central Virginia.
episodes.168940: Thunderstorms produced scattered instances of damaging winds and large hail, some considerable, across extreme eastern West Virginia into northern and central Virginia.
episodes.169035: A north-south stationary boundary bisected central Pennsylvania ahead of a cold front approaching from the Great Lakes on June 16, 2022. A broken line of showers and thunderstorms formed along a lake-breeze front that developed over northwestern Pennsylvania, just ahead of the approaching cold front. As this line progressed southeastward, one of the cells within the line became a long-track supercell that produced a swath of wind damage and hail from Warren County southeastward to the Lower Susquehanna Valley.
episodes.169045: As a heat wave ensued across the Central Appalachians during the middle of June, the atmosphere remained primed for afternoon showers and thunderstorms. On June 16th, the strongest storms resided across the northern portions of West Virginia, where numerous trees were blown down and quarter sized hail fell. A few instances of heavy downpours within the storms occurred, leading to high water along local roadways in Tyler and Gilmer Counties.
episodes.169055: Afternoon showers and thunderstorms quickly got underway across southeast Ohio on June 16th as abnormally warm temperatures were in place. A few storms grew to become strong to severe, resulting in damaging winds that knocked down trees in the towns of Reinersville and Lower Salem. Heavy downpours were also observed within activity that afternoon, which caused flash flooding to be observed along the Duck Creek and Lower Muskingum River in Washington County.
episodes.169072: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms ongoing across the South Carolina Upstate and Midlands region produced a strong cold pool which led to convection following a south-southeast path into portions of southeast South Carolina during evening hours.
episodes.169242: A line of thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon across western Wisconsin and tracked through northeast Wisconsin through the evening hours on Wednesday (6/15).  The storms formed into a Quasi-Linear Convective System (QLCS) with multiple reports of damaging winds of 70 to 80 mph as well as 10 tornadoes embedded within the main line of thunderstorms.  The 10 tornadoes ties a record for the most tornadoes in an event for northeast Wisconsin.  Additional storms late in the evening produced a few reports of large hail near the lakeshore as they moved offshore.  ||The swath of damaging winds caused multiple power outages, with over 125,000 customers without power across northeast Wisconsin.  Power was not restored for several days across many areas as the cleanup from the storms took an extended period of time.
episodes.169461: A line of thunderstorms moved southeast across Lake Michigan, bringing strong thunderstorm winds during the early morning hours.
episodes.169474: A pre-frontal surface trough axis drifted southeastward across northeast OH, northwest PA, and western NY during the afternoon of the 16th. In addition, a surface cold front drifted southeastward across Lake Erie and into northeast OH, northwest PA, and western NY during the afternoon through early evening as an occluded low drifted eastward across southern Hudson Bay. The pre-frontal surface trough axis, cold front, and a Lake Erie lake breeze front in northeast OH and northwest PA acted as foci for the development of multicells and supercells. These storms encountered moderate to strong effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively, as they evolved generally eastward or east-southeastward in the warm sector. There were multiple reports of severe hail and damaging convective wind gusts.

episodes.169560: A line of storms moved across Lake Michigan from Wisconsin during the evening of 6/15, producing wind gusts in excess of 34 kts that were measured near the lakeshore.
episodes.169756: A cold front moving through a moist and unstable airmass spawned a line of particularly strong severe thunderstorms over portions of south central Upper Michigan on the evening of the 15th.
episodes.169773: A severe squall line formed along a surface trough and brought numerous swaths of wind damage to southern WI. Tree damage was prevalent and some structural damage occurred. The line of storms also slowed down, causing sporadic street flooding. Two home fires occurred after being struck by lightning.
episodes.169807: Thunderstorms moving through Saginaw Bay and southern Lake Huron produced wind gusts around 40 knots.
episodes.169808: Two lines of thunderstorms tracked through southeast Michigan during the early morning hours. Scattered severe thunderstorms were embedded in each line.  Damaging winds brought down trees and lead to power outages, especially hard hit was Bay, Oakland, and Livingston counties.
episodes.169856: Clusters of severe thunderstorms resulted in several areas with wind damage and an isolated tornado across portions of the Pee Dee region.
episodes.169878: A broken line of strong to severe storms, including some supercells, moved through eastern Iowa, northeast Missouri, and northwest Illinois the evening of June 15th. These storms produced wind damage and large hail.
episodes.170010: A MCC (mesosclae convective complex) formed in the region late in the day on the 15th. This system brought storms across the Northern Tier in Northeastern Pennsylvania. One storm became severe along the eastern PA/NY border and knocked down multiple trees in Manchester Township in Wayne County.
episodes.170012: A MCC (mesoscale convective complex) developed over west-central New York late in the day on the 15th. This system swept across Central New York after midnight on the 16th, triggering multiple storms. Some of the storms became severe with damaging wind gusts being the main hazard.
episodes.170013: After storms early in the morning, a cold front brought another round of showers and thunderstorms to Central New York during the day. A warm airmass helped create an unstable environment and supported severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170142: A stationary frontal boundary extending from southern Lake Michigan to northern Missouri triggered a line of strong to severe thunderstorms across north-central Illinois during the early morning of June 16th.  One of the cells within the line became severe, producing wind damage and quarter-sized hail across Woodford County.
episodes.170714: A unusual summer-time upper air pattern developed across the Central Gulf Coast states  with an upper high centered just north of Alabama. Several upper level impulses rotated around the eastern side of the high and produced clusters of severe storms that tracked westward across Central Alabama.
episodes.170732: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms moved through areas of northern Missouri, into central Missouri. The storms went well into the overnight hours producing scattered instances of damaging winds, along with a few marginally severe hailstones.
episodes.170782: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a warm front produced damaging winds, large hail, and three tornadoes across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.170854: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the Georgia mountains during the evening. One of the storms produced large hail in Rabun County.
episodes.170855: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon and moved southeast. Some of the storms organized into small clusters. Several of the clusters and individual cells produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170858: Scattered thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon and moved southeast. Some of the storms organized into small clusters. Several of the clusters and individual cells produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170860: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northeast Georgia during the afternoon. One of the storms produced large hail in Rabun County.
episodes.170890: A large slow moving supercell thunderstorm sat over Lyon County during the evening of 6/15, which lead to flash flooding near Hartford, KS.
episodes.170968: A line of severe thunderstorms produced strong winds over the bay of Green Bay and the Lake Michigan waters during the early evening hours on Wednesday (6/15).  Another round of thunderstorms produced large hail later in the evening over the Lake Michigan nearshore waters.
episodes.171161: A ridge over the Tennessee Valley contributed to an extremely hot and humid environment over North Carolina. There was anomalously high instability in the area as well. This instability combined with an approaching outflow boundary from a complex of thunderstorms to the north, helped trigger widespread showers and thunderstorms. Several of these storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.171356: A very active summer pattern resulted in numerous reports of trees and power lines down across the tri-state area.  Most of the damage occurred on June 14th as a large MCS moved south and southwestward across most of the area.

episodes.171484: An isolated slow moving storm moved across portions of east central Kansas producing a short lived EF0 tornado and flash flooding in and around the community of Madison.
episodes.171592: The Lake Ontario lake breeze sagged southward early in the evening and intersected an enhanced cumulus field residing over eastern Erie, eastern Niagara, Genesee, Wyoming, and Livingston counties. At the same time, a subtle short wave trough aloft crossed over the aforementioned area. Capping had kept robust instability at bay through the afternoon until the combination of these features was finally able to allow convective initiation. The storms then busted through the cap and aided by 35-40 knots of shear, the storms grew rapidly and managed to maintain intensity.
episodes.171593: The Lake Ontario lake breeze sagged southward early in the evening and intersected an enhanced cumulus field residing over eastern Erie, eastern Niagara, Genesee, Wyoming, and Livingston counties. At the same time, a subtle short wave trough aloft crossed over the aforementioned area. episodes.171594: The bulk of the area was ensconced within a very warm and sultry air mass with dewpoints of 70-75 degrees. This allowed for a very unstable air mass that was also highly sheared. While a cold front was bearing down on the region from Ontario, most of the severe weather was initiated along a lake breeze that pushed east from Lake Erie. The thunderstorms that initiated developed very strong cores aloft and were responsible for several large hail reports of up to golf ball size. Additionally, the strongest storms of the day ripped through the Genesee Valley. Those storms were surveyed by a team from the NWS, and winds of 100 mph were estimated to be responsible for the damage found there.

episodes.171625: An occluded front interacted with a hot and humid air mass to produce a cluster of showers and thunderstorms that moved east across central North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. These storms resulted in widespread wind damage across roughly the western half of the region. There was also a report of flash flooding in Stanly County.
episodes.171639: A line of strong thunderstorms traversed Lake Michigan, eventually moving across the eastern Upper Peninsula and into Ontario, Canada. While this line produced severe wind gusts over land, it also produced a measured wind gust of 41 mph at Point Iroquois.
episodes.171641: A seasonably strong trough progressed from the northern Great Plains over the Midwest on 6/15, providing ample forcing aloft to support convective initiation along a cold front stretching across portions of WI, MN, and IA during the afternoon. These storms quickly grew upscale into a line that continued to travel northeast through the evening. Eventually, these storms tracked across portions of the northwest Lower Peninsula and the eastern Upper Peninsula, producing marginally severe hail and damaging wind gusts late in the evening.
episodes.171798: A multi-day severe weather event unfolded mid June as multiple disturbances surrounding the outer periphery of a mid level high pushed through an abnormally moist environment and highly unstable environment over the forecast area. These storms produced numerous reports of trees & powerlines down, quarter to golf ball size hail, structural damage, and isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.171843: A mesoscale convective system moving southwest across Georgia and Alabama on 6/15 decayed just after midnight as it moved through Alabama. The residual feature continued southwest through the morning hours of the 16th. Daytime heating reinvigorated the system across southeast Louisiana in the afternoon hours. One storm intensified enough to produce damaging wind gusts.

events.narrative: The NWS storm survey team observed widespread damage from Faithorn to Hermansville with several structures severely damaged and thousands of trees uprooted or snapped off.  Downed trees and powerlines resulted in impassable roads. |The NWS survey team also concluded that the damage was characteristic of intense straight line winds of 100 to 110 mph.  This is supported by radar data which showed a classic descending rear inflow jet (strong high altitude winds descending to the ground) surging northeastward across this area. In addition, the downed trees fell in mainly the same direction along with signs of divergent flow in the damage pattern.

The tornado formed in a wooded area west of Lawson Grove Rd, then caused tree damage as it crossed Lawson Grove Rd. The tornado continued toward the southeast and flipped a large agricultural irrigation system in a corn field along Joja Rd. Next, the tornado crossed Philadelphia St. and caused damage to trees before causing minor flashing and roof shingle damage at the Philadelphia Methodist Church. It also destroyed an outdoor storage building and knocked down a few granite headstones in the adjacent graveyard. The tornado continued toward the southeast across fields and a forest south of Philadelphia St. Finally, the tornado weakened as it moved across S Center Rd where it ripped a metal roof off a single wide mobile home and caused minor roof damage to a home on the east side of S Center Rd as it lifted.

A second tornado in Fluvanna, Goochland and Powhatan counties developed from a second circulation behind the initial tornado. The track paralleled the EF1 tornado with damage noted from south of Kent Store to south of Maidens and into northern Powhatan county. Several trees were uprooted or snapped, and there was minor structural damage in Fluvanna county. The tornado tracked from Fluvanna county into Goochland county.
